summary: Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at SFSU and UCLA under William R. LaFleur. She served as a professor at Princeton (1990–2019) and president of the SSJR (~1996–1999).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. Her career includes posts at the University of Manchester, where she was attested in 2005 and as an Honorary Research Fellow in 2026.

Jacques André (1910–1994) worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Jules Marouzeau. He held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot (1877–1965) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot, later serving there as directeur d’études (1935–1938) and as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

Jacques David Ehni (1827–1903) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen. He later held posts at the Lyceum of Ludwigsburg and Humboldt-Gymnasium Ulm.

Jacques Gernet (1921–2018) worked in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at EFEO, EPHE/EHESS, the University of Paris, Paris Diderot University, and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès (1950–2021) specialized in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at ENSBA and Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne and École du Louvre, and served as Chief Curator and President at Guimet Museum.

Jacques Leider is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO under Denise Bernot, Paris-Sorbonne, and the University of Luxembourg under Pierre L. Lamant. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and joined the EFEO in 2001.

Jacques Maritain (1882–1973) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Henri-IV, the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Henri Bergson (~1901–1904), and the University of Notre Dame. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1940–1944).

Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Constantin Régamey, served as editor-in-chief at Hōbōgirin (~1968–1981), and was a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1962–1992).

Jacques Scheuer (1942–2021) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts at Centre Sèvres and Université catholique de Louvain (~1978–2007).

Jacques van Ginneken (1877–1945) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America (1923) and Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1945).

Jacques-Albert Cuttat (1909–1989) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studying at the universities of Bern and Paris. He held posts at the University of Bern (1935), Columbia University (~1946–1948), and as Professor of Philosophy at the Sorbonne.

Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was a historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Patna College, BHU, and Ravenshaw College, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Jae-gwon Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2007 and subsequently held a post there.
Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indologist who served in the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, where his posts are attested from 1924 to 1930 and as Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji (b. 1875) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned a B.A. at the University of Cambridge and served as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911).

Jagannath Upadhyaya worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at CIHTS in 1985.

Jagdish Kashyap (1908–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Patna College, BHU, and Vidyalankara Pirivena under Rahul Sankrityayan. He held posts at BHU, founded and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, and taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Jaideva Singh (1893–1986) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Swami Lakshman Joo, Srikrishna Harihirlekar, and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He was chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).
